findings.problem: Prev/next buttons labeled with exercise name abbreviation ('Bench', 'Squat', etc.) but text color is --color-muted and size is xs (tiny). Disabled buttons use opacity-30 (very faint). Dot indicator shows current exercise but user may not realize it's clickable.
findings.impact: On mobile during a tiring workout, user can't quickly see 'am I on exercise 2 of 5?'. Button labels are hard to read. Disabled state is too subtle—user might tap a disabled button and think the app froze.
findings.fix: Increase button font size to sm. Disabled state: use text-muted/50 + clearer styling (e.g., 'opacity-50'). Add larger, more visible exercise counter '2/5' in center dot section. Show full exercise name in a tooltip on hover (desktop) or in a brief modal (mobile).

findings.problem: Finish button only appears on last exercise. User has to navigate all the way to the end to finish—no visible 'Finish anytime' affordance. SessionSummary component handles post-workout view but is not visible during session (details tag in page.tsx, line 238).
findings.impact: User may not realize they can finish early or abandon a session. Modal/dismissible patterns are unclear. Finish-session UX is hidden behind a details toggle.
findings.fix: Show 'Finish workout early' button (secondary variant) on all exercises, not just last. Expand SessionSummary details tag by default or move summary to floating card. Add 'Save & Exit' / 'Abandon session' modal options.

findings.problem: Weight label ('×0.5', '×1.0', '×2.0') shown as small muted badge. Habit name truncates with no visual hierarchy. Completed streak emoji + number (🔥 5) is appended inline. Empty state shows hint text 'Tap = check, drž = vrátit zpět.' but long-press is not visible/discoverable in the actual habit row.
findings.impact: User doesn't understand XP multiplier system (weight). Hint text contradicts missing affordance. No visual difference between checked/unchecked states except checkbox + text fade.
findings.fix: Habit name: bold, larger. Weight badge: rename to 'XP ×1.0' with explanation (tooltip on hover). Completed state: add light accent background to row + strikethrough on name. Show visible 'Undo' button on checked state (not long-press). Streak: keep emoji but larger, right-aligned.

findings.problem: Empty state text: 'Zatím nemáš žádné návyky.' + 'Tap = check, drž = vrátit zpět.' The second line is a hint for future use but appears before any habit is created. It's confusing and contradicts the lack of UI to tap.
findings.impact: New user is confused: 'Tap what?' and 'Hold to undo what?'. Hint is premature and creates cognitive dissonance.
findings.fix: Replace hint text with clear CTA: 'Start building better habits — tap below to create your first one.' Only show gesture hints after habits are created (in the actual habit list).

findings.problem: Optimistic UI updates checkbox locally but refreshes entire page (router.refresh()) on success/error. No toast confirmation visible to user—error toast shows but success is silent. Uncheck flow shows 'Vráceno' info toast—that's the only feedback that undo worked.
findings.impact: User doesn't know if habit check was saved. Network latency feels like lag. Success is less rewarding than error—error gets a toast, success gets a silent refresh.
findings.fix: Keep optimistic UI. Add success toast: 'Hotovo!' or 'Zvládl jsi!' (Czech idiom). Show streak milestone message on first uncheck of the day (if XP awarded), then uncheck. Add haptic feedback.

findings.problem: Reward card shows 'Vyzvednout' (redeem) button with disabled state when user doesn't have enough XP. Disabled button shows title='Chybí X XP' on hover but button is styled with reduced opacity (hard to see). No visual indication of how close user is to redemption.
findings.impact: User taps 'Vyzvednout' on an expensive reward and gets a silent error or error toast. No progress bar or visual 'X more XP needed' indicator. Feels blocked/uninformed.
findings.fix: Replace disabled button with secondary variant button + red text 'Chybí 250 XP'. Add progress bar showing current balance vs. reward cost (e.g., '500 / 750 XP'). Show it on the card, not just on hover.

findings.problem: Empty state shows 'Žádné odměny' with CTA 'Vytvoř si první odměnu' button. But there's also a '+ Nová odměna' button at the top of the page (RewardsPageClient.tsx, line 99). Two CTAs for the same action. Icon is a generic Gift icon, not motivational.
findings.impact: User seeing empty state doesn't know if they should use the button on the empty state or the one at the top. Redundant CTAs feel messy. No context about what rewards are for.
findings.fix: Remove button from empty state. Instead show: 'Žádné odměny' + description 'Co si chceš dopřát za odvedenou práci? Vytvoř si první odměnu a používej ji jako motivaci.' CTA at top stays. Keep single, clear button placement.

findings.problem: Redeem API returns 'Insufficient balance' error but code shows generic alert('Nedostatek XP'). No visual affordance in the dialog to see current balance before confirming. User must cancel, check balance, then retry.
findings.impact: User redeems reward, gets error, has to backtrack. Two-tap problem where one tap should suffice. No clear UI showing 'you need X more XP'.
findings.fix: RedeemConfirmDialog should show current balance and cost before confirm button. Add a progress indicator: 'Your balance: 500 XP / Cost: 750 XP'. Disable confirm button if insufficient. Show 'You need 250 more XP' message instead of error.

findings.problem: Stats page titled 'Avatar Progress' (line 31) but sections are generic: 'Avatar Progress', 'Muscle Rank', 'XP History'. No clear 'this is your RPG character progression' theme. Avatar card and tier ladder shown but no story/narrative about tiers or muscle ranks.
findings.impact: Gamification concept feels disconnected. User doesn't understand tier progression (bronze → silver → gold) or what muscle ranks represent. Stats page feels data-heavy, not motivational.
findings.fix: Rename to 'Your Journey' or 'Character Progress'. Add lore/descriptions: 'You are level X — a [Tier Name]. Unlock higher tiers by earning XP.' Show tier benefits on TierLadder (e.g., 'Silver: Unlock advanced stats'). Add muscle rank explanations: 'Chest: Rank 3 — Strong development'.

findings.problem: Sparkline cards shown in horizontal scroll. Labels are generic ('Váha', 'Pas', 'Hrudník'). No clear which goal is 'lower-is-good' (weight) vs 'higher-is-good' (chest). MeasurementGrid is a dense table with all columns visible—hard to scan on mobile.
findings.impact: User sees sparklines but doesn't know if trending up or down is good. Dense table is unreadable on phone. No visual guidance on how to interpret trends.
findings.fix: SparklineCard: add subtle arrow or color indicator (🟢 down / 🔴 up based on goal). MeasurementGrid: make responsive—show only current week + last week on mobile, full table on desktop. Add 'Goal: lower weight' label in sparkline legend.

findings.problem: Bio page shows sections but no clear narrative. 'Vitals', 'Goal', 'Lifetime', 'Transformation' are all present but disconnected. No visual progress toward goal (e.g., weight loss target). Transformation strip shows photos but no comparison UI.
findings.impact: User sees stats but doesn't feel connected to their progress story. No 'you've come X% toward your goal' celebration. Photos are a feature but not integrated into progress narrative.
findings.fix: Add 'Goal Progress' section at top: show current vs goal weight with progress bar + '8kg lost of 15kg goal (53%)'. Show first photo vs recent photo side-by-side on Transformation section. Add 'Milestone: X weeks on journey' badge.

findings.problem: Calendar legend shown but symbols are not immediately clear. Empty state says 'Začni svoji cestu — první session, habit nebo váha se tu objeví.' No visual affordance or link to create first session/habit/measurement from calendar.
findings.impact: New user lands on calendar, sees blank month, reads message, but doesn't know where to click to start. No CTA buttons pointing to training/habits/progress pages.
findings.fix: Add three small CTA buttons below empty state: 'Start training' → /training, 'Create habit' → /habits, 'Log weight' → /progress. Show calendar legend prominently above grid with color-coded explanations.

findings.problem: Active sidebar link styled with accent color + left border. Inactive links are muted text. But muted color (#6b7280) is very gray on dark background—hard to distinguish from disabled/inactive state. No hover feedback is visible.
findings.impact: User scanning sidebar can't quickly identify current page. Hover state (hover:text-foreground) is there but very subtle. On mobile (bottom-nav), active tab is accent-colored but inactive tabs are hard to see.
findings.fix: Active link: keep accent + left border, but also add subtle accent background (e.g., bg-accent/5 or bg-surface-raised). Inactive: keep muted text. Hover: add visible bg-surface lift. Bottom-nav inactive tabs: increase size or add subtle label highlight.

findings.problem: Login form is minimal—just email + password inputs and a submit button. No brand identity or context. No password recovery link. Error message is generic ('Neplatný email nebo heslo'). Loading state shows only text ('Přihlašuji…') with no visual feedback (spinner, disabled state clarity).
findings.impact: User unsure if they're in the right place. No way to recover lost password. If sign-in takes time, user doesn't know app is responding.
findings.fix: Add Hexis logo or title at top. Show 'Forgot password?' link below password field. Add loading spinner to button during sign-in. Keep error message but add password reset CTA: 'Zapomněl jste heslo? Kontaktujte podporu.'

findings.problem: Loading fallback is plain text 'Načítám…' (line 133, ExerciseStepper). No skeleton screen, no progress indicator. Error boundaries are missing—if a page crashes, user sees blank or cryptic error (e.g., 'Session nenalezena' on line 38 of workout/[sessionId]/page.tsx). No retry affordance.
findings.impact: User sees 'Loading...' with no ETA or sign that something is happening. If data load fails, user is stuck with an error message and no way to recover except refresh.
findings.fix: Add skeleton loaders for ExerciseStepper, measurements grid, and other async sections. Show error states with retry button: 'Chyba při načítání. Zkus znovu.' Add global error boundary (ErrorBoundary component) with option to clear data or contact support.

findings.problem: App has no onboarding flow. New user logs in directly to dashboard. No guided setup: profile (name, height, weight goal, gender), no plan selection, no first habit creation. User sees data cards with numbers but no context on how to use them.
findings.impact: New user is completely lost. No guidance on 'what should I do first?'. App feels finished/static, not inviting. No hook to create first session or habit. High abandonment rate.
findings.fix: Create multi-step onboarding (or use modal wizard): 1) Welcome/intro 2) Profile setup (name, height, goal weight, gender) 3) First plan selection or create ad-hoc session 4) First habit creation 5) Dashboard tour (what is XP, level, tier?). Store onboarding state in user prefs, show once. Consider in-context tooltips on dashboard elements.

findings.problem: Muted text is --color-muted #6b7280 on dark background #0a0e14. WCAG contrast ratio ~4:1 (borderline). Small text (xs, 10px) + muted color is hard to read. Section labels, secondary text, disabled buttons, hints—all use this color. Eye strain on prolonged reading.
findings.impact: User has to squint to read secondary information. Section titles ('Life Areas', 'Daily Habits') are hard to scan. Accessibility fails WCAG AA standard for normal text. Feels cheap/low-effort design.
findings.fix: Increase muted text contrast: use #9CA3AF instead of #6b7280 (contrast ~6:1). For section labels, use text-sm instead of text-xs, keep weight 500. For hints/tertiary text, increase opacity to 70%. Test all text combos for WCAG AA compliance.

findings.problem: Dialog component exists but is used sparingly. Skip dialog in ExerciseStepper is modal but has no close-on-background affordance. No visual cue that it's dismissible. BottomSheet and other overlays may lack consistent styling/affordance.
findings.impact: User doesn't know they can tap outside the dialog to close. If they want to cancel without choosing, they have to find the dismiss button. Feels trapping.
findings.fix: All dialogs: add semi-transparent scrim, allow scrim tap to dismiss (unless critical action). Add visible X or back button at top-left. Consistent border/shadow treatment. Document in design system.

findings.location: src/components/ui/compound/Toast.tsx (not shown); multiple API success/error flows
findings.problem: Toast notifications appear to dismiss after a few seconds. Success toasts are silent (user doesn't know operation succeeded). Error toasts are shown but are easy to miss/dismiss. No queue behavior—if two toasts fire, they may overlap.
findings.impact: User isn't sure if an operation succeeded. Errors disappear before user reads them. Stacked toasts clutter the screen.
findings.fix: Success toast: keep visible 3-4 seconds, or show 2-second toast + persistent inline feedback. Error toast: keep visible 5+ seconds, or require explicit dismiss. Show toast queue stack on top-right, max 3 visible. Use distinct colors (green success, red error, blue info).

findings.problem: Primary variant button uses accent color (amber #f59e0b). Secondary is primary border (green #10b981). On dark theme, both colors are bright and equally dominant. Disabled state reduces opacity to 50%—very subtle. No clear visual hierarchy between primary, secondary, danger actions.
findings.impact: User can't quickly identify the primary action. Disabled buttons look like they might still be clickable (just less bright). On small screens, button text may wrap awkwardly.
findings.fix: Primary button: accent background (current). Secondary: border only, no fill. Danger: red background. Disabled: grayscale + strikethrough or lock icon. Test button hierarchy on mobile with thumb-reachability in mind.

findings.problem: NumberInput likely uses HTML input type='number'. On mobile, opens numeric keyboard. But mobile numeric keyboards don't always include decimal point without extra taps. Increment/decrement buttons (if present) may be tiny on small screens.
findings.impact: User entering weight (e.g., 22.5 kg) has to tap extra times to find decimal. Feels clunky. No clear feedback on what step size is (step={2.5} in SetInput).
findings.fix: NumberInput: show large +/− buttons on mobile (or up/down swipe). Use inputMode='decimal' for weight/cm inputs. Show step size as label: '22.5 kg (step 2.5)'. For reps, use integer input with clear 1-rep steps.

findings.problem: Bottom navigation only shows 4 items (dashboard, training, progress, stats) — 6 major sections (nutrition, habits, rewards, bio, calendar, settings) are completely hidden on mobile with no alternate mobile-friendly navigation
findings.impact: Mobile users cannot directly navigate to nutrition tracking, habits, rewards, bio, settings, or calendar. They must drill through the profile menu or guess nested routes. Major app features are essentially invisible on phones.
findings.fix: Either: (a) expand MOBILE_TABS to include all or most areas with smaller font/icons, (b) add a 5th/6th tab with submenu, or (c) add a hamburger menu alongside the bottom nav for secondary areas. Current design abandons half the feature set on mobile.

findings.problem: App layout uses md: breakpoint for sidebar with no responsive padding adjustment. Mobile main content has pb-16 (bottom nav), desktop has pb-0, but the jump is abrupt at 768px. No tablet/mid-size phone intermediate state.
findings.impact: At 767px (mobile), full width is used. At 768px (tablet), sidebar suddenly appears but desktop assumes mouse + hover states. No smooth transition. Tablet users get desktop layout with touch inefficiency.
findings.fix: Add sm: and lg: breakpoints with progressively revealed sidebar. At sm (640px), show collapsed sidebar icon bar. At lg (1024px), show full sidebar. Replace hard md: boundary with incremental reveals.

findings.problem: Life Areas section uses grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4. On mobile, this is 2 columns; on desktop, 4 columns. On a typical iPhone (375px), 2 columns leaves ~160px width per card, forcing text wrapping and cramped layout.
findings.impact: Card labels (TRAINING, NUTRITION, etc.) are 2xl bold and compete with small viewport width. Visual hierarchy is flattened. On very narrow phones (320px-375px), text wraps and card feels cluttered.
findings.fix: Use responsive text sizes: text-lg sm:text-2xl on value, shrink secondary text to text-[10px] on mobile. Consider grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 or allow cards to stack on very narrow screens without losing prominence.

findings.problem: Calendar grid is strictly grid-cols-7 with no responsive behavior. Each cell is aspect-square with fixed padding p-1. On mobile ≤375px, each cell is ~50px wide, making text (dayNum class='text-sm') nearly unreadable and signal dots (h-[6px] w-[6px]) invisible.
findings.impact: Calendar is functionally broken on small phones. Day numbers are tiny, dots are invisible, tapping small cells is error-prone. Users cannot reliably see which days have workouts or habits.
findings.fix: On mobile, show a month view with text-[10px] for day numbers and hide signal dots, or switch to a vertical date list. Alternatively, use responsive padding (p-0.5 on mobile, p-2 on tablet) and make the grid 7 columns only on md+.

findings.problem: Nutrition calendar is also grid-cols-7 with fixed px-4 padding. Calendar day cells are clickable but offer no size hint. On 320px screens, effective cell width is ~30px, making them ~30x30px — below 44px touch target minimum.
findings.impact: Touch targets are too small. Users will miss-tap frequently. Especially problematic on the nutrition tracking page where daily input is core workflow.
findings.fix: On mobile, reduce grid columns dynamically or switch to vertical list view of days. If keeping grid, ensure min touch target of 44x44px even if columns reduce to 4–5 on mobile.

findings.problem: Measurement table is fixed width with no horizontal scroll hint. Table has 8 columns (Tyden, Vaha, Δ, Pas, Hrudnik, Stehno, Biceps, kcal cil). On mobile, the outer div has overflow-x-auto p-4, but no visual cue that the table scrolls. Text in headers is text-[11px] and right-aligned, making it hard to parse. MeasurementCell inputs are likely too cramped horizontally.
findings.impact: Table is scrollable but users don't know it. On small screens, most columns are off-screen initially. Cognitive load is high; users must scroll horizontally repeatedly to enter data. Touch target widths for cell inputs are unknown but likely small.
findings.fix: Make table visually 'scrollable' with a scroll indicator or gradient fade on right edge. On mobile (<640px), show only 3–4 most important columns (Week, Weight, Δ) and collapse others into a detail view. Or use a card-per-week layout instead of a grid for mobile.

findings.problem: Workout stepper uses flex flex-col gap-4 p-4 with no max-width constraint. On large phones/tablets, this can stretch to full width, making long exercise names and set displays very wide. NumberInput buttons are h-11 w-11, which is 44x44px (good), but the layout doesn't constrain width, so inputs stretch awkwardly on large screens.
findings.impact: On a 700px-wide tablet, the exercise card and input fields stretch full width, reducing visual focus. Long exercise names don't wrap well. The 'Zapsat sérii' button is also full-width and ungainly.
findings.fix: Wrap the stepper content in a max-w-md or max-w-lg container on tablet/desktop. On mobile, keep full-width. Add responsive width constraints and ensure SetInput layout is compact on narrow screens (flex-col on mobile, flex-row on tablet).

findings.problem: Stepper prev/next buttons use only px-2 padding, no minimum height. ChevronLeft/ChevronRight are size 14. Button text is text-xs. Effective button height is likely 24–28px, below 44px standard touch target.
findings.impact: Small buttons are hard to tap on mobile. Requires precise finger accuracy during an active workout, which is disruptive.
findings.fix: Set minimum height h-10 or h-11 on both nav buttons. Increase icon size to size-5 and add vertical padding (py-2) to reach 44px target.

findings.problem: Photo grid uses grid-cols-3 with no responsive breakpoint. On mobile 320px, each cell is ~100px. Photos are aspect-square with relative sizing; touch target is okay, but text below (PoseBadge) may be cut off or hard to read at small sizes.
findings.impact: Photo thumbnails are very small on phones. Pose badges are hard to read. User cannot quickly identify which photos belong to which pose/date without visual clarity.
findings.fix: Use responsive grid: grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3 md:grid-cols-4 or add lg: breakpoint. Increase text size for pose badge on mobile (text-[8px] → text-[9px] minimum). Consider full-width card layout on mobile with larger thumbs.

findings.problem: Upload button is position fixed right-4 bottom-20 z-30. On mobile with bottom nav (h-16 = 64px), bottom-20 (80px) places the FAB 80px from bottom, which is 16px above the nav. This leaves only 16px margin. On landscape (272px height), the FAB may overlap the nav or be inaccessible.
findings.impact: FAB may be hidden behind the bottom nav on small screens or landscape. Users cannot easily upload photos on mobile in landscape mode.
findings.fix: Adjust bottom offset dynamically: bottom-20 on portrait, bottom-4 md:bottom-20 on landscape. Or use safe-area-inset-bottom: bottom-[calc(1rem+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))] to account for notches and nav.

findings.problem: Month navigation uses ChevronLeft/Right (size 24) in px-4 buttons with no responsive min-width or height. On mobile, the button is likely 24x24 + padding, totaling ~40x40px, below 44px standard.
findings.impact: Navigation buttons are slightly undersized. Users may miss-tap, especially in landscape or on older phones with poor touch accuracy.
findings.fix: Set minimum button dimensions: h-10 w-10 or h-11 w-11. Ensure ChevronLeft/ChevronRight remain size-6 (24px) within the padded button.

findings.problem: HabitDailyRow uses flex items-center gap-3 rounded-lg border px-3 py-2.5. The checkbox is size-5 (20px), and the row height is effectively ~36–40px (py-2.5 = 10px top+bottom, text-sm line-height ~20px). This is below 44px recommended touch target. On TodaysChecksCard, rows are stacked in a space-y-2 gap, so vertical spacing is minimal.
findings.impact: Habit checkboxes are small and easy to mis-tap. The 'Otevřít' link at the bottom of TodaysChecksCard is text-primary text-sm, inheriting small touch target from surrounding text.
findings.fix: Increase py to py-3 (12px) to reach ~44px row height. Increase checkbox size to size-6. Ensure the 'Otevřít' link is inside a min-height-11 or use a proper Button component with h-10 minimum.

findings.problem: Reward cards and dialog buttons (if present) use standard button sizing, but the full reward card row may be compressed. No specific responsive behavior for rewards on mobile.
findings.impact: Reward cards may look okay at small sizes, but if multiple are shown, the layout could feel crowded. Buttons inside dialogs may be small on mobile.
findings.fix: Ensure all buttons in reward dialogs are h-10 or h-11 minimum, and use responsive text sizing (text-base on mobile, text-sm on desktop if needed).

findings.problem: BioHero uses flex items-center gap-4 with Avatar tier=tier size=96. On mobile 320px, a 96px avatar + name + right-aligned 'Day' column compresses significantly. The 'Day' number is text-3xl, but the entire row may wrap or overflow unexpectedly on very narrow screens.
findings.impact: Avatar is too large for small phones (96px on a 320px screen is 30% of width). Text may wrap into the Day number or day number may be pushed off-screen.
findings.fix: Use responsive avatar size: Avatar size={64} sm:size={96}. Allow Day section to drop below avatar on mobile (flex-col on mobile, flex-row on sm+). Or truncate 'Day' to just the number with text-2xl sm:text-3xl.

findings.problem: TransformationStrip shows Then/Now in grid grid-cols-2 gap-3. Images are set to w-full on mobile (correct), but the outer gap-3 and padding may cause images to be cramped. At 320px width with gap and borders, actual image width is ~140px, making then/now photos very small.
findings.impact: Transformation photos are tiny on mobile, defeating their purpose as motivational visual feedback. Hard to see physical changes.
findings.fix: On mobile, use grid-cols-1 to stack Then/Now vertically, giving each photo ~280px width. Switch to grid-cols-2 at sm+ breakpoint.

findings.problem: Dialog uses w-[min(92vw,420px)], which is good, but fixed top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 centers the dialog absolutely. On a small phone in landscape (say 667px width, 375px height), the dialog is centered but may push content off-screen vertically or be visually cramped.
findings.impact: Dialogs on landscape phones can be cramped vertically. No consideration for very narrow screens or keyboard pop-up (on iOS, this can shrink viewport by 50%).
findings.fix: Use a BottomSheet-style dialog on mobile (md and below), centering only on desktop. Implement responsive positioning: sm:top-1/2 for desktop, relative positioning for mobile. Or ensure Dialog has max-height with overflow-y-auto to stay within viewport.

findings.problem: BottomSheet is fixed right-0 bottom-0 left-0, which is correct, but uses p-4 pb-8 with no adjustment for mobile keyboard or safe-area-inset-bottom. On iPhone with notch/home indicator, pb-8 (32px) may not be enough space below content.
findings.impact: BottomSheet content may be partially hidden under home indicator or keyboard on mobile. Users cannot scroll content fully.
findings.fix: Change pb-8 to pb-[max(2rem,env(safe-area-inset-bottom)+1rem)] or use dynamic spacing. Ensure max-height with overflow-y-auto so content is scrollable even if keyboard appears.

findings.problem: Progress page shows 5 SparklineCard components in a flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto pb-2. Each card is min-w-[140px], so 5 × 140px = 700px total, forcing horizontal scroll on mobile. The scroll is not visually obvious (no scrollbar indicator, no gradient fade). On 320px screen, only ~2.3 cards are visible, and users must discover the scroll.
findings.impact: Users don't realize there are more measurements to view. The horizontal scroll pattern is not obvious on mobile without a visual cue (scrollbar, fade gradient, or animated nudge).
findings.fix: Add a right-edge gradient fade (using a pseudo-element or overlay div with pointer-events-none) to hint scrollability. Or reduce card min-width on mobile: min-w-[100px] sm:min-w-[140px]. Or make cards stack vertically on mobile (flex-col sm:flex-row).

findings.problem: Avatar is rendered as inline-block with size={96} sm:size={64} not applied. The size prop is hardcoded per context (e.g., StatusWindow uses size=140), with no responsive adjustment. On large phones in landscape, a 140px avatar is overkill.
findings.impact: Avatar is disproportionately large on some screens, taking up too much space. Less impactful but noticeable in compact layouts.
findings.fix: Pass a responsive size hint (e.g., size='large' → {mobile: 80, tablet: 120, desktop: 140}) or use inline style with media query logic. Or accept size as a breakpoint object: {mobile: 64, sm: 96, md: 140}.

findings.problem: Root layout applies dark theme and basic styling, but does not account for iOS notch/safe area at the top. Many pages use py-4 or py-6 for padding but no pt-[env(safe-area-inset-top)]. On iPhone with notch, content may touch the notch.
findings.impact: On iPhone X/12/14+, content may visually overlap the notch, reducing readability of headers and titles. Low severity but affects premium feel.
findings.fix: Add pt-[env(safe-area-inset-top)] to key containers (Container, AppShell main, or header). Or use viewport-fit=cover with inset safety padding.

findings.problem: Based on pattern, strength page likely has charts (OneRmChart, VolumeChart, StagnationList). Charts are often fixed-width (e.g., width: 600px), and on mobile ≤375px, they overflow horizontally without scrolling or responsive sizing.
findings.impact: Charts are cut off or illegible on mobile. Users cannot see their strength progress data on phones.
findings.fix: Ensure all charts use responsive width: width: min(100%, 600px) or width: 100% with max-width: 600px. Add overflow-x-auto if chart must maintain aspect or data density. Or simplify chart on mobile (fewer data points, smaller font sizes).

findings.problem: Header shows 'Life · <Area Name>' with hidden text on mobile (hidden md:inline). On very narrow phones, even '<Area Name>' may be truncated. The header layout is flex justify-between, so the user menu is pushed to the right. On 320px, the area label may wrap or be cut off.
findings.impact: Users don't know which section they're in on mobile. Orientation context is lost.
findings.fix: Use responsive text sizes: text-[10px] sm:text-xs for area label. Or ellipsis overflow: {label}. Ensure area label is always visible even on 320px screens, possibly by moving user avatar to a different position or reducing header content.

findings.problem: Design uses --font-sans with system fonts, but no webfont is actually loaded (Inter is listed in fallback but not @imported). Rendered font depends on OS default: -apple-system on iOS, Segoe UI on Windows, Roboto on Android. Metric variations between these fonts are significant, potentially breaking tight layouts. Additionally, no responsive font-size scaling is defined at the root level, so text sizes are fixed across all screens.
findings.impact: Text rendering differs by device, causing layout shifts. Small text (text-[10px], text-[11px]) may be barely readable on older phones with lower DPI. No baseline font scaling for accessibility.
findings.fix: Either load a webfont (e.g., @import 'fonts/inter.css') for consistency, or add responsive font-size scaling: html { font-size: 14px; } @media (min-width: 640px) { font-size: 16px; }. This scales all rem-based sizing proportionally.

findings.problem: AppShell hardcodes flex min-h-screen flex-col md:pl-[220px]. The sidebar is completely hidden on mobile (hidden md:flex), and users must use the bottom nav. The bottom nav only shows 4 tabs, forcing access to other sections via menu. This is a dead-zone on mobile: the sidebar is invisible, the bottom nav is limited, and header dropdown is the only fallback — poor UX.
findings.impact: Critical navigation gap on mobile. Users cannot quickly jump to nutrition, habits, rewards, bio, or calendar. Must use header menu (slow) or know deep links (bad discoverability).
findings.fix: Add a mobile-optimized navigation: either expand bottom nav to 5–6 items (with icon-only labels), add a hamburger menu, or create a slide-out drawer from left/right. Bottom nav must provide access to all primary sections or there must be a fallback nav system.
